cases.name: install-new-approval-required
cases.description: First install of a new id by its single covering publisher.

cases.name: install-new-admit
cases.description: The same request with a bound operator approval commits a tombstone, ownership, grants and targets; the install stays disabled until a separate enable.

cases.name: identical-retry
cases.description: Equal publisher, manifest, package, grants and targets for an active install return the existing install.

cases.name: identical-bytes-different-targets
cases.description: Identical bytes with other targets and no grant_update flag are refused and point to a grant update.

cases.name: identical-bytes-different-grants
cases.description: Identical bytes with another grant proposal and no grant_update flag are refused and point to a grant update.

cases.name: reinstall-after-uninstall
cases.description: A tombstoned version that is not installed may be reinstalled with identical bytes and a new approval.

cases.name: upgrade-approval-required
cases.description: A new version of an installed id is an upgrade.

cases.name: upgrade-admit
cases.description: Upgrade with a bound approval; the new pair gets a tombstone, ownership already exists and the enabled state carries over.

cases.name: rollback-to-tombstoned-version
cases.description: Returning to an earlier accepted version while another is installed is an upgrade whose tombstone must match.

cases.name: grant-update-approval-required
cases.description: A target change on an installed version is a grant update through the same stages.

cases.name: grant-update-admit
cases.description: The approved grant update writes new generations and targets; no tombstone or ownership is created.

cases.name: grant-update-not-installed
cases.description: A grant update needs an active install of exactly this version.

cases.name: grant-update-all-devices-refused
cases.description: A GitOps target write cannot reach all devices; only the server image may use that target.

cases.name: retired-key-grant-update-narrow
cases.description: The publisher key was retired after install; narrowing the running install needs no current publisher authority.

cases.name: retired-key-grant-update-narrow-admit
cases.description: The approved narrowing commits under the retired key.

cases.name: retired-key-grant-update-widens-grant
cases.description: Under a retired key a grant update may not widen a component, even within the manifest request.

cases.name: retired-key-grant-update-adds-group
cases.description: Under a retired key a grant update may not reach a device group the install does not target.

cases.name: revoked-key-grant-update-refused
cases.description: A revoked key never authorizes a grant update; only retirement is relaxed.

cases.name: grant-update-exceeds-request
cases.description: A grant update stays within the manifest request like an install.

cases.name: single-administrator-admit
cases.description: With approval policies disabled the coordinator records an exemption for the requester; nobody approves, and the intent names the exemption.

cases.name: single-administrator-operator-still-accepted
cases.description: A second principal may still approve in a single-administrator installation.

cases.name: single-administrator-unavailable
cases.description: The exemption is refused while approval policies are enabled.

cases.name: single-administrator-other-principal
cases.description: An exemption is recorded for the requester only; another principal uses the operator kind.

cases.name: single-administrator-closure-change
cases.description: Disabling approval policies changes the closure, so an approval requested before it is stale.

cases.name: single-administrator-policy-revert
cases.description: An exemption bound before approval policies were enabled and disabled again stays stale: the setting's generation advanced.

cases.name: approval-over-other-grants
cases.description: An approval bound to the wider proposal does not authorize a narrowed proposal; narrowing is a new request.

cases.name: first-start-release-fixed-install
cases.description: During first-start setup no device group exists; the server image installs and enables a project-signed adapter for all devices.

cases.name: first-party-release-fixed-upgrade-equal
cases.description: A later server release upgrades a first-party component without an operator when no grant widens and the targets are unchanged.

cases.name: release-fixed-version-mismatch
cases.description: A release-fixed approval names the running release, which must equal the package version.

cases.name: first-party-upgrade-keeps-narrowed-targets
cases.description: An operator narrowed the adapter to one group; the release upgrade keeps that target without an operator.

cases.name: first-party-upgrade-restores-all-devices
cases.description: A release request that would move a narrowed install back to all devices needs an operator.

cases.name: first-party-upgrade-keeps-disabled
cases.description: An operator disabled the adapter; the release upgrade installs the new version and leaves it disabled.

cases.name: first-party-grant-update-narrow
cases.description: An operator narrows the grant of a fleet-wide first-party adapter; the grant update keeps all devices because the install already targets them.

cases.name: first-party-grant-update-narrow-admit
cases.description: The approved narrowing commits with all devices kept, the same binding and the enabled state unchanged.

cases.name: retired-key-grant-update-all-devices-to-groups
cases.description: Under a retired key, moving a fleet-wide install to device groups is a narrowing and is accepted as under an active key.

cases.name: first-party-grant-update-retarget-groups
cases.description: The operator may also move a fleet-wide install to device groups; it may never move a group install to all devices.

cases.name: first-party-upgrade-after-grant-narrowing
cases.description: Starting from the commit of first-party-grant-update-narrow-admit, the release grant is wider than the stored grant, so the upgrade needs an operator.

cases.name: first-party-release-fixed-upgrade-widened
cases.description: A widened first-party grant needs an operator approval.

cases.name: first-party-widened-operator-admit
cases.description: An operator approves the widened release proposal for the same digest; a server-image request keeps all devices.

cases.name: single-administrator-server-image
cases.description: The exemption never covers a server-image request: its requester is the system principal, so the one administrator approves as an operator.

cases.name: first-party-reinstall-after-uninstall
cases.description: An operator uninstalled the adapter; the next start cannot reinstall it without an operator.

cases.name: first-party-install-after-uninstall
cases.description: After an operator uninstall, a later release's version is a new install that needs an operator.

cases.name: first-party-new-id-after-first-start
cases.description: A first-party id that first ships in a later release is proposed by the server image and needs an operator.

cases.name: first-party-new-id-operator-admit
cases.description: The operator approves the server-image proposal; it installs for all devices and stays disabled until enabled.

cases.name: first-party-recovery-pending-reinstall
cases.description: After an epoch transition the server image re-asserts its component with a release-fixed approval, bounded by the pre-transition grants and targets.

cases.name: first-party-recovery-with-new-release
cases.description: A recovery_pending install at an older version meets a new release: the upgrade case admits it within the pre-transition grants and targets.

cases.name: development-build-release-fixed-refused
cases.description: An unsigned build has no running release, so a release-fixed approval is refused even for the matching development label.

cases.name: development-build-proposal
cases.description: After setup closed the first-start marker, the unsigned build proposes its first-party component without a release-fixed approval; it waits for an operator.

cases.name: development-build-operator-admit
cases.description: An operator approves the development build's proposal after first start; it installs for all devices and stays disabled until enabled.

cases.name: purged-project-key-not-recreated
cases.description: The project key was retired and purged; start-up loading treats its purge floor as present and does not re-create it, so a server-image request finds no key.

cases.name: first-party-recovery-targets-changed
cases.description: Re-assertion keeps the operator's narrowed targets; a request for all devices needs an operator.

cases.name: recovery-pending-reinstall
cases.description: After an epoch transition the same bytes need a new request; nothing is relabelled.

cases.name: prior-owner-reinstall-after-transfer
cases.description: A prior owner may reinstall exactly the version it published before the transfer.

cases.name: prior-owner-rollback-upgrade
cases.description: The prior-owner exception covers every operation on a version whose tombstone names the key, including a rollback over the new owner's version; the operator approves it.

cases.name: retired-prior-owner-resolves
cases.description: A retired trust entry stays on the list, so ownership records and tombstones that name it keep resolving.

cases.name: key-unknown
cases.description: The publisher fingerprint is not on the trust list.

cases.name: key-invalid
cases.description: A trust entry whose raw key fails Ed25519 admission authorizes nothing, even when the fingerprint matches.

cases.name: key-revoked
cases.description: A revoked publisher key is refused before any namespace or tombstone check.

cases.name: key-retired
cases.description: A retired trust entry authorizes no admission until re-imported.

cases.name: namespace-reserved
cases.description: A non-project key cannot publish under io.ricevanta; both namespace defects are reported.

cases.name: namespace-prefix
cases.description: The id lies outside every prefix of the verifying key.

cases.name: namespace-lookalike-not-reserved
cases.description: io.ricevantaevil is an ordinary id; prefix matching ends at a label boundary.

cases.name: revocation-id
cases.description: A revoked id refuses every version.

cases.name: revocation-version
cases.description: A revoked version refuses only that version.

cases.name: tombstone-package-mismatch
cases.description: Same manifest bytes in a different archive are different bytes for the pair.

cases.name: tombstone-publisher-and-manifest
cases.description: Another publisher cannot reuse an accepted pair; every mismatch is listed.

cases.name: ownership-assignment-required
cases.description: Two trust keys cover the id; a protected assignment must exist first.

cases.name: ownership-revoked-entry-still-covers
cases.description: A revoked covering entry still counts, so an immediate unprotected revocation cannot decide who owns a new id.

cases.name: ownership-retired-entry-does-not-cover
cases.description: A retired entry does not cover, so after a protected retirement the remaining key takes ownership of a new id.

cases.name: ownership-retired-entry-admit
cases.description: The admitted install creates ownership for the one non-retired covering key.

cases.name: ownership-assigned
cases.description: With an assignment the owner publishes under overlapping prefixes.

cases.name: ownership-owner-mismatch
cases.description: A covering key that does not own the id cannot publish a new version.

cases.name: transferred-prior-owner-new-version
cases.description: After a transfer the prior owner cannot publish new versions.

cases.name: interface-unserved
cases.description: The server names the interface version it does not serve.

cases.name: component-verdicts
cases.description: Every component needs a passing validator verdict.

cases.name: registration-unknown
cases.description: An adapter must reference a stored browser registration.

cases.name: registration-intersection
cases.description: Requests outside the registration's names, native-host targets or OS list fail.

cases.name: registration-bound
cases.description: One adapter per browser registration across the installation while its holder is active.

cases.name: registration-bound-recovery-pending-holder
cases.description: A binding held by a recovery_pending install does not block; the new install rebinds on commit.

cases.name: registration-rebind-admit
cases.description: The intent names the registration binding the coordinator writes at commit.

cases.name: registration-duplicate-in-package
cases.description: Two adapters in one package name one unbound registration; every adapter after the first is refused.

cases.name: registration-duplicate-pending-holder
cases.description: The same holds when a recovery_pending install holds the registration.

cases.name: registration-duplicate-unknown
cases.description: The duplicate check does not depend on the registration being stored: the second adapter carries both codes.

cases.name: identical-retry-set-order
cases.description: Set-valued grant arrays compare as sets: a proposal listing the same policy names in another order is an identical retry.

cases.name: identical-retry-outbound-order
cases.description: Outbound tuples are a set ordered by their JCS bytes: the stored canonical order and the proposal's manifest order are one grant.

cases.name: request-digest-set-order
cases.description: Both digests canonicalize set-valued arrays, so an approval of the sorted proposal admits the reordered one.

cases.name: upgrade-drops-adapter-releases-binding
cases.description: An upgrade whose new version has no adapter commits an empty binding set; the coordinator releases the id's old binding.

cases.name: upgrade-renames-adapter-same-registration
cases.description: A binding held by the same id never blocks: the new binding set replaces the id's bindings, so a renamed adapter keeps its registration across the upgrade.

cases.name: upgrade-moves-adapter-registration
cases.description: An upgrade that moves the adapter to another registration binds the new one; the old binding, absent from the set, is released.

cases.name: targets-device-groups-required
cases.description: Agent-bound components need device groups, or all devices on a server-image request.

cases.name: targets-all-devices-and-groups
cases.description: all_devices and device groups exclude each other.

cases.name: targets-all-devices-not-server-image
cases.description: An upload cannot target all devices, so no approval request is created that no approval could satisfy.

cases.name: targets-unknown-group-and-console
cases.description: Unknown groups and a console target without a console module are refused together.

cases.name: targets-connector-forbids-device-groups
cases.description: A connector-only package targets jobs and no device group.

cases.name: grant-missing-and-extra
cases.description: Every component has exactly one proposed grant.

cases.name: grant-kind-mismatch
cases.description: A grant must carry its component's kind and interface.

cases.name: grant-registration-mismatch
cases.description: A browser-adapter grant names the component's registration.

cases.name: grant-exceeds-request
cases.description: A grant value above the requested value is refused.

cases.name: grant-narrower-than-request
cases.description: A requester may propose less than the manifest requests.

cases.name: grant-collector-profile-and-roots
cases.description: Collector grants need a reviewed disclosure profile and at most max_roots roots.

cases.name: mixed-package-approval-required
cases.description: Console, connector and collector components with narrowed grants.

cases.name: grant-console-slot-not-requested
cases.description: A slot the manifest did not request cannot receive operations.

cases.name: approval-digest-mismatch
cases.description: An approval bound to other request bytes does not authorize this request.

cases.name: approval-separation
cases.description: Requester and approver must differ for the operator kind.

cases.name: approval-consumed
cases.description: A consumed approval never authorizes a second commit.

cases.name: approval-epoch
cases.description: An approval that names a prior recovery epoch is stale even when its digest matches.

cases.name: approval-stale-closure
cases.description: A revocation of another version of the id after approval advances the id's revocation generation, so the approval is stale.

cases.name: approval-revocation-revert
cases.description: A version revocation added and removed after approval leaves the approval stale; it never revives.

cases.name: approval-enabled-revert
cases.description: An install disabled and re-enabled after an upgrade approval has a new install generation, so the approval stays stale.

cases.name: approval-trust-entry-revert
cases.description: A publisher key revoked and then unrevoked after approval has a new entry generation, so the approval stays stale.

cases.name: approval-release-fixed-not-project
cases.description: Only the project publisher on a reserved id from the server image may use a release-fixed approval.

cases.name: approval-release-fixed-wrong-source
cases.description: A project-signed package uploaded by an operator still needs an operator approval.

cases.name: precedence-key-before-tombstone
cases.description: A revoked key hides later defects; the package mismatch is not reported.

cases.name: input-snapshot-duplicate-fingerprint
cases.description: Rule 1: fingerprints are unique on the trust list.

cases.name: input-snapshot-fingerprint-key-mismatch
cases.description: Rule 2: a trust entry's fingerprint is the SHA-256 of its raw key.

cases.name: input-snapshot-revocation-other-id
cases.description: Rule 3: every revocation names the id under decision.

cases.name: input-snapshot-revocation-other-version
cases.description: Rule 3: a version revocation in the snapshot names the version under decision.

cases.name: input-snapshot-ownership-other-id
cases.description: Rule 4: the ownership record names the id under decision.

cases.name: input-snapshot-tombstone-other-id
cases.description: Rule 5: every tombstone names the id under decision.

cases.name: input-snapshot-duplicate-tombstone
cases.description: Rule 5: at most one tombstone per version.

cases.name: input-snapshot-install-other-id
cases.description: Rule 6: the install names the id under decision.

cases.name: input-snapshot-install-without-tombstone
cases.description: Rule 6: the installed version has a tombstone with the same package digest.

cases.name: input-snapshot-install-duplicate-component
cases.description: Rule 7: the install's grant records name distinct components.

cases.name: input-snapshot-grant-record-identity
cases.description: Rule 7: each grant record carries the install's id, version and package digest.

cases.name: input-snapshot-active-install-old-epoch
cases.description: Rule 8: an active install's grant records carry the snapshot epoch; an older epoch means recovery_pending.

cases.name: input-snapshot-grant-record-later-epoch
cases.description: Rule 8: no grant record carries an epoch above the snapshot's.

cases.name: input-snapshot-duplicate-registration
cases.description: Rule 9: one registration record per registration id.

cases.name: input-snapshot-owner-missing
cases.description: Rule 10: the owner is an entry on the trust list.

cases.name: input-snapshot-prior-owner-missing
cases.description: Rule 10: every prior owner is an entry on the trust list.

cases.name: input-snapshot-imported-project-flag
cases.description: Rule 11: only the entry whose fingerprint is the binary's compiled project key carries project_publisher.

cases.name: input-snapshot-project-key-unflagged
cases.description: Rule 11: the entry for the compiled project key carries project_publisher.

cases.name: input-snapshot-tombstone-publisher-missing
cases.description: Rule 10: every tombstone publisher is an entry on the trust list.

cases.name: input-snapshot-tombstone-without-ownership
cases.description: Rule 12: a tombstone exists only beside the id's ownership record.

cases.name: input-snapshot-install-without-ownership
cases.description: Rule 12: an install exists only beside the id's ownership record.

cases.name: input-request-duplicate-grant
cases.description: Two grants for one component are a malformed request.

cases.name: input-request-server-image-operator
cases.description: A server-image request names the system principal as its requester.

cases.name: input-request-system-principal-upload
cases.description: The system principal requests only as the server image.

cases.name: input-request-system-principal-approver
cases.description: The system principal never approves and never holds an exemption.

cases.name: input-request-server-image-grant-update
cases.description: The server image never writes grants on an installed version.

cases.name: input-evidence-invalid-document
cases.description: A document that fails manifest validation yields no evidence.
